about: Sealed messages, sealed media, the peek frame, signed SDP, and which keys an event can trust: docs/API.md (Sealed messages, Realtime, Events).

A message is {"sealed": base64url(0x04 || epoch (u32, big-endian) || nonce(12) || ciphertext || tag(16))}: AES-GCM under the epoch's petcam.box.v1 key over the message's JSON, with `context` as associated data. 0x02 || nonce || ciphertext || tag, with no epoch, is epoch 0.

Media is 0x05 || epoch (u32, big-endian) || nonce(12) || ciphertext || tag(16): AES-GCM under the epoch's petcam.media.v2 key, with `context` as associated data. 0x03 (the same layout) and 0x01 (no epoch) under petcam.media.v1 with no associated data are from before 2026-11-03, and no longer open.

Sealing draws a random nonce; the ones here are fixed (cast.mjs derives each from its vector's name), so an implementation that seals `plaintext` for `context` with `nonce` gets `sealed` byte for byte. JSON is compared as values, never as text: key order and how a number is written may differ.

`expect` is "opens", or how it fails: "refused" (it doesn't authenticate, or is too short to), "unknown_version" (not a format the apps open), "stale_keys" (an older epoch, where only the current one counts), "newer_keys" (an epoch past the newest held: catch up on the home's keys, then try again), "unknown_keys" (an epoch never held, or not the one its event names).

`worker_takes` says what the server's shape check makes of it (docs/API.md: base64url, version byte, length). It can't open anything, so everything sealed passes unless it says false, altered or not; `not_sealed` is what it must refuse.
Bytes are base64url without padding unless a field says hex or base64; strings are UTF-8; "|" joins the parts of a message, with nothing around it.
HKDF is HKDF-SHA256 with salt "petcam" and 32 bytes out; HMAC is HMAC-SHA256; AES-GCM is AES-256-GCM with a 12-byte nonce and a 16-byte tag.

Made by server/scripts/vectors.mjs from fixed keys that were made up for these files; nothing here was ever a real home's. No vector is ever removed: a format the apps stop opening stays, as one that must fail. Read by SharedTests/SealedVectorTests.swift and server/test/vectors.test.ts.

holders.how: Which epochs each device here holds, and when it took each (ms, by its own clock). Its current epoch is its newest.

contexts.how: The associated data of each kind of sealed thing: UTF-8, never sent.

signal.what: A signal's payload, from the viewer to the camera for one session

command.what: A command, from the viewer to the camera

invite_token.what: An invite's token, sealed for the household

account.what: A device's word for its account

person.what: The name of the person signed in on a device

device_name_not_ascii.what: A name that takes more than one byte a character

device_name_epoch_0.what: A device's name under the epoch before

device_name_v02.what: A device's name as builds from before keys could change sealed it: 0x02, no epoch (epoch 0)

command_epoch_0.what: A command under the epoch before: what a removed device that kept old keys could seal

event_details_epoch_0.what: An event's details under the epoch before

home_name_epoch_2.what: The home's name under a newer epoch

event_details_epoch_2.what: An event's details under a newer epoch

peek.what: A camera's peek frame: peek_frame.packed inside

snapshot_epoch_0.what: A snapshot under the epoch before

empty.what: Nothing inside: the shortest media there is, 33 bytes

unbound_v03.what: As builds before 2026-11-03 sealed media: 0x03, under petcam.media.v1, bound to nothing

unbound_v01.what: As the first builds did: 0x01, no epoch (epoch 0), under petcam.media.v1, bound to nothing

peek_frame.how: Before it is sealed: when the camera captured it (ms since 1970, u64 big-endian), the JPEG, then zeros to 32,768 bytes. Unpacking drops every zero after the last other byte (a JPEG ends FF D9).

also.what: A frame from before padding: the time and the JPEG, nothing after
Too short to hold a time and anything else

fits.how: A JPEG fits a frame when 8 + its length is at most 32,768; a busier picture is encoded again, smaller.

event_trust.how: An event is listed only when its details open and count: their epoch and their media's (media_epoch, else the details' own) are at least the newest epoch this device had taken more than ten minutes before the event started, and the media's is no newer than the details'. `event` is as the server lists it; `counts` says whether it is listed, and `media_epoch` which epoch its snapshot and clip must then be under.

cases.name: before_the_keys_changed
cases.why: it started before this device took epoch 1: epoch 0 is what a camera had then

cases.name: within_the_grace
cases.why: five minutes after: a camera still catching up, or a clock a little off

cases.name: at_the_end_of_the_grace
cases.why: ten minutes after, to the millisecond: still allowed

cases.name: just_past_the_grace
cases.why: a millisecond past ten minutes: details under epoch 0 no longer count

cases.name: older_keys_after_the_change
cases.why: what a removed device seals, with the keys it kept, for a time after the home moved on

cases.name: newer_keys_after_the_change
cases.why: the camera's own, under the new keys; its media is under the details' epoch

cases.name: new_details_old_media
cases.why: new details naming media under the old keys, for a time after the change: the media could be anyone's who kept them

cases.name: parked_across_the_change
cases.why: an event that waited in the outbox across the change: details under the new keys, media under the keys of when it started

cases.name: media_newer_than_details
cases.why: media under a newer epoch than its details: no camera makes that

cases.name: under_keys_not_held_yet
cases.why: sealed under epoch 2, which this device hasn't caught up on: not listed until it has

cases.name: moved_in_time
cases.why: listed at another time than its details are sealed to

cases.name: no_times_kept
cases.why: a device whose saved keys carry no times (from before devices kept them) holds nothing back

not_sealed.how: What the server must refuse wherever a sealed message or sealed media belongs: plaintext, and anything too short to be sealed.
